statement: The function returns a result r and r = (sum_{i=0}^{n-1} popcount(nums[i])) + max_{i=0}^{n-1} top(nums[i]).
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. For a nonnegative integer x, popcount(x) is the number of 1 bits in its binary expansion, and top(x) is 0 if x=0 and otherwise the index of its highest set bit; thus top(0)=top(1)=0, top(2)=1, and so on.

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail, overflow, or panic.
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} popcount(nums[i]).
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. For a nonnegative integer x, popcount(x) is the number of 1 bits in its binary expansion.

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= 30*n + 29.
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and nums[i]=0 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} nums[i].
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, nums[i] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let ys be the array of length n-1 obtained by deleting nums[j], so ys[i]=nums[i] for 0 <= i < j and ys[i]=nums[i+1] for j <= i < n-1. Then the function returns a result r and r = the result returned by min_operations(ys).
preconditions: nums has length n with 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and nums[j]=0 for some j with 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let ys be the array of length n defined by ys[i]=nums[p(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < n. Then the function returns a result r and r = the result returned by min_operations(ys).
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Also p is a permutation of {0,...,n-1}.

statement: Let xs be such an array. Then the function returns a result r and r = (the result returned by min_operations(xs)) + 1.
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. There exists an array xs of length n with 0 <= xs[i] <= 500000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n, nums[i]=2*xs[i] for every i, and xs[j] > 0 for at least one j.

statement: The function returns a result r and there exists a call sequence of length r from the zero array to nums that uses exactly S increment calls and exactly T doubling calls, where S = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} popcount(nums[i]) and T = max_{i=0}^{n-1} top(nums[i]).
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. statement: The function returns a result r and for every k >= 0 and every sequence of k calls, where each call is either adding 1 to one chosen coordinate or doubling every coordinate, that starts from the all-zero array of length n and ends at nums, we have r <= k.
preconditions: nums has length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.
